narrative:
On November 4, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded a total hearing rate of 40.5%, with 1,282 cases heard out of 3,167 scheduled. This performance is consistent with recent historical trends, tracking slightly higher than the 40.1% observed on October 16 and significantly above the 38.8% reported on October 15. The court maintained a balanced procedural environment, with a marginal bias gap of 0.9% between government and commoner case hearings.

Judge-wise performance showed significant variability across halls. High clearance rates were observed in Hall 31 (C.M. Poonacha, 80% heard rate for specific blocks) and Hall 23 (V. Srishananda, 79.4%). Conversely, some high-volume dockets, such as Hall 7 (B.M. Shyam Prasad), experienced lower immediate clearance, with segments recording a 2.5% hearing rate despite a high volume of 118 scheduled cases.

Analysis by hearing stage reveals that Admissions (43.4%) and Orders (43.2%) continue to command the highest throughput, while Final Hearings remain at a lower conversion rate of 29.4%. This aligns with the historical pattern observed in mid-October, where Final Hearings consistently represented the most significant procedural bottleneck compared to pre-hearing stages.

Case-type distribution confirms that Writ Petitions (WP) remain the primary administrative burden, accounting for 1,406 of the scheduled matters with a 37% hearing conversion. Notably, high-clearance niche categories included WPHC (100%) and CP (100%), while staple categories like CRL.P and MFA recorded hearing rates of 41.3% and 43.2%, respectively. The consistency of these figures suggests a stable operational capacity within the court for managing diverse case types alongside evolving scheduled dockets.
